instructional_purpose: Establishes comparison (التشبيه) as an analysable object with a fixed inventory of named slots, so that a learner decomposes a comparison into labelled parts instead of only registering its effect. Adds a naming scheme that classifies any comparison by which of the two optional slots have been left out.
concepts_taught: comparison as a four-slot analytic frame
the two obligatory poles versus the two optional slots
the comparison exponent as a set spanning a prefixed particle, an independent noun and adjectival forms
case licensed by the exponent: genitive after the prefixed particle, accusative in the كأنّ frame
binary classification by presence or absence of the exponent (مرسل / مؤكد)
binary classification by whether the shared quality is verbalised (مفصل / مجمل)
the doubly-omitted composite type (بليغ) and the claim that omission strengthens the assertion
asymmetry of the two poles: the second pole is the more familiar or more vivid one

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A comparison decomposes into two obligatory poles plus an optional exponent and an optional expression of the shared quality; removing an obligatory pole ends the comparison rather than reclassifying it within the scheme.
The prefixed comparison particle governs genitive on the noun it attaches to.
The كأنّ frame assigns accusative to the noun that follows it, in contrast to the genitive assigned by the prefixed particle.

Exponents of comparison are not a single part of speech: the inventory includes a prefixed particle, an independent noun heading a genitive annexation, and adjectival or participial forms taking a prepositional complement.
Omission of the exponent is interpreted as asserting identity rather than as neutral compression.
The scheme is presented as five types although it is two independent binary parameters plus their doubly-negative combination.

The explicit statement of the shared quality is identified with a prepositional adjunct, yet the lesson's own walkthrough also accepts a bare attributive adjective in that role without noting the widening.
A predication with no exponent remains a comparison, not a metaphor, as long as both poles are present in the clause.

recognition_criteria: a one-letter prefixed comparison particle standing before a genitive noun
an independent comparison noun heading an annexation
the كأنّ frame introducing a clause with an accusative first term
a bare nominal predicate naming a category the subject cannot literally belong to, with no exponent present
a prepositional adjunct naming an abstract quality attached to the comparison
both poles recoverable inside the same clause
procedures: identify the two poles by asking what is being described and what it is set against
test for an exponent and assign the exponent-presence label
test whether the shared quality is verbalised and assign the explicitness label
combine the two labels, or assign the doubly-omitted label when neither is present
rehearse the whole sequence on one fully worked comparison with each slot named
conditions: both poles must be recoverable for the comparison classification to hold at all
the exponent must be overt for the exponent-present label
the shared quality must be verbalised for the detailed label
exceptions: an unexponented predication is still a comparison, not a metaphor, when both poles are present
the exponent may surface as a noun or an adjective, so exponent detection cannot be reduced to matching one letter
contrasts: exponent present versus exponent omitted
shared quality stated versus left to inference
comparison versus metaphor decided by how many poles survive
plain literal description versus comparison

common_mistakes.pattern: swapping the two poles, treating the vivid or familiar term as the thing being described
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the roles are not symmetric; the described term is the one the speaker wants to characterise, the other supplies the characterising image
common_mistakes.correction_principle: assign roles from communicative intent, asking which term the discourse is actually about, not from word order alone

common_mistakes.pattern: calling the doubly-omitted type a metaphor because no exponent appears
common_mistakes.why_wrong: exponent absence is not pole absence, and the class boundary is drawn on pole count
common_mistakes.correction_principle: test whether both poles can be pointed to in the clause before leaving the comparison class

common_mistakes.pattern: ignoring a prepositional adjunct that names the shared quality and treating it as ornament
common_mistakes.why_wrong: that adjunct is the slot that decides the detailed versus implicit label
common_mistakes.correction_principle: scan for an abstract-quality adjunct before assigning the implicit label

common_mistakes.pattern: putting the wrong case on the noun after the exponent
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two frequent exponents license opposite cases, so the case is diagnostic and not free
common_mistakes.correction_principle: let the exponent's own governance decide the case rather than copying the case of a neighbouring noun

proposed_new_units.summary: A discriminator over comparison configurations: four named slots, two binary parameters (exponent present or absent, shared quality verbalised or not), the composite labels they generate, and the exponent inventory with the case each exponent licenses.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: No catalogue unit covers rhetorical figure classification; the only genuine overlap with u-n02 and u-n03 is the governance fact about the كأنّ frame and the prefixed particle, which is a small licensing addition and leaves the slot-and-type scheme homeless.

instructional_purpose: Extends the comparison frame by deleting one of its two obligatory poles and names the two resulting configurations by which pole survives. Introduces the contextual signal that blocks the literal reading and directs recovery of the deleted pole.
concepts_taught: metaphor (الاستعارة) as a comparison with one obligatory pole deleted
the explicit type: the image-pole survives, the described pole is deleted
the implied type: the described pole survives and the image-pole is recoverable only from a property attributed to it
the blocking clue (القرينة) that forbids the literal reading and points at the deleted pole
the borrowing terminology: the borrowed word, what it is borrowed for, what it is borrowed from
the boundary test separating the doubly-omitted comparison from explicit metaphor
a graded progression from fully exponented comparison to fully implicit metaphor

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Metaphor is derived from comparison by deleting one obligatory pole; the exponent is necessarily absent as well.
In the explicit type the surviving pole is the image; in the implied type the surviving pole is the described thing and the image is inferred from a property predicated of it.
A figurative reading is licensed only when some element makes the literal reading untenable, and that same element directs recovery of the deleted pole.
The deletion is semantic recoverability, not syntactic ellipsis: nothing in the sentence's case marking or agreement records the missing pole, so it is recovered from the clue alone.
The blocking clue is typed into verb-based, noun-based, action-based and context-based varieties.
A predication whose two poles are both present remains a comparison even with no exponent, so pole count and not exponent absence decides the class.
The lesson presents a both-poles-present specimen under the explicit-metaphor heading and then retracts the classification in place, leaving a self-corrected item inside its own worked inventory.
Increasing implicitness increases rhetorical force, ranking the four configurations on a single scale.

recognition_criteria: a nominal denoting a category incompatible with its predicate or with the action around it
a predicate or attribute drawn from a semantic field alien to its stated subject
no comparison exponent anywhere in the clause
no second pole locatable in the clause, which selects the explicit type
a stated subject accompanied by an alien attribute whose true owner is never named, which selects the implied type
procedures: locate the expression that resists a literal reading
ask what is being described and what it is being set against
ask whether the image is named openly
if the image is named openly and the described pole is absent, assign the explicit type
if the described pole is named and the image survives only inside an attributed property, assign the implied type
name the blocking clue and state which pole it recovers
conditions: one pole must be genuinely absent, not merely unexpressed by an exponent
the attributed property in the implied type must belong to a different semantic field from the stated subject
the clue must be present, otherwise the sentence is an ordinary statement
exceptions: a predicate that is literally compatible with its subject yields no metaphor even when it feels figurative
both poles present blocks the metaphor classification regardless of exponent absence
contrasts: explicit versus implied by which pole survives
metaphor versus the doubly-omitted comparison by pole count
alien-field predicate versus literally compatible predicate
the resemblance basis of this figure versus other figurative mechanisms taught later in the module

common_mistakes.pattern: reading a doubly-omitted comparison as an explicit metaphor because both look like bare nominal predication
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the two classes differ by whether a pole is genuinely absent, not by whether an exponent is absent
common_mistakes.correction_principle: try to point at both poles in the clause; if both can be pointed at, the case stays in the comparison class

common_mistakes.pattern: labelling an expression as implied metaphor without identifying the clue that recovers the deleted image
common_mistakes.why_wrong: with no clue there is no deletion to recover and the sentence is simply a statement
common_mistakes.correction_principle: require an explicit named clue before assigning the implied type

common_mistakes.pattern: treating every verb used of an inanimate or abstract subject as an implied metaphor
common_mistakes.why_wrong: many such predicates are literally true of that subject and involve no transfer at all
common_mistakes.correction_principle: check that the predicate genuinely belongs to another semantic field before assigning any figurative label

common_mistakes.pattern: interchanging the three borrowing labels
common_mistakes.why_wrong: they name three different things — the borrowed word, its target of application, and its source concept — and differ only by a following particle
common_mistakes.correction_principle: fix each label by the question it answers: which word, applied to what, taken from what

proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n08 covers structure that is syntactically absent but grammatically recorded, such as governed gaps and estimated elements with case consequences; here nothing is recorded in the parse and the missing pole is recovered by world knowledge alone, so mapping this onto hidden-structure would be domain resemblance rather than coverage.

instructional_purpose: Introduces the third figure of the imagery science, defined not by deletion or by resemblance but by the survival of a coherent literal reading alongside an intended further meaning. Splits it into three subtypes according to what the indirect expression points at, and makes the inference chain from surface to intent explicit.
concepts_taught: الكناية defined by the continued possibility of the literal reading
subtype pointing at a quality (كناية عن صفة)
subtype pointing at an unnamed entity (كناية عن موصوف)
subtype attributing a quality to a person through something annexed to them (كناية عن نسبة)
the stepwise inference chain from observable state to intended meaning
the paired labels for the alluding expression and the thing alluded to
shared cultural knowledge as a precondition for successful decoding
the evidential character of the figure: the literal statement functions as proof of the inferred quality

linguistic_propositions.proposition: The figure is defined by the compatibility of the literal reading with the intended one; if the literal reading must be rejected, the case leaves this class.
Three subtypes are distinguished by the target of the allusion: an attribute, an entity, or an attribution routed through a possession or associate.
The surface expression carries evidential force, so that the literal state of affairs is offered as proof of the inferred quality rather than as a mere label for it.
Whether this figure counts as literal usage or as a species of figurative usage is disputed among rhetoricians; only the reading on which the literal sense remains available is presented.
The entity-pointing subtype is illustrated with an animal name applied to a person, a case that mainstream treatments class as resemblance-based metaphor rather than as this figure.

The relation subtype is extended to a case where the quality is attributed to an inanimate plural and intended for a collective, whereas the classical formulation routes the attribution through something annexed to a single person.
Decoding depends on culture-specific encyclopaedic knowledge; without it the inference chain fails and the expression is taken literally.
The same figure is used both to name what politeness or elegance discourages naming directly and to add sensory content that a bare name would not carry.

recognition_criteria: an adjective annexed to a body-part or possession noun where the literal reading remains coherent
a definite descriptive phrase standing in the syntactic slot a proper name would occupy
an abstract quality noun predicated as located in or upon something belonging to a person
a literally true statement that would be uninformative if meant literally in its context
a conventionalised multi-token expression whose reading is fixed by usage rather than composed
procedures: test whether the literal reading is possible; a possible literal reading keeps the case in this class
state the intended meaning explicitly
classify by whether the target is a quality, an entity, or an attribution via something related
reconstruct the inference chain one step at a time from observable state to intended conclusion
check that the required cultural premise is actually available
conditions: the literal reading must remain coherent
a conventional or contextually inferable chain must connect the literal state to the intended meaning
the audience must share the cultural premise the chain relies on
exceptions: expressions whose literal reading is impossible fall outside the class and belong to metaphor
a general statement with no inferable further meaning is simply literal description
contrasts: this figure versus metaphor decided by whether the literal reading survives
quality-pointing versus entity-pointing subtypes, that is an adjective-like target versus a noun-like target
direct attribution to a person versus attribution routed through a possession
showing through evidence versus telling by naming

common_mistakes.pattern: classifying an expression as metaphor when its literal reading is perfectly coherent
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the class boundary is exactly the survival of the literal reading
common_mistakes.correction_principle: run the literal-possibility test first and let its outcome select the class

common_mistakes.pattern: reading the entity-pointing subtype label as though it named a quality
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the label names the thing described, that is a noun-like target, not the description
common_mistakes.correction_principle: ask whether the intended meaning is a thing or a property, and let the answer pick the subtype

common_mistakes.pattern: stopping at the literal paraphrase in the relation subtype and leaving the quality attached to the possession
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the attribution is meant to transfer from the possession to its owner
common_mistakes.correction_principle: finish the chain by carrying the quality across the relation to the person

common_mistakes.pattern: expecting the expression to be decodable from its words alone
common_mistakes.why_wrong: many instances are idiomatic and rest on culture-specific premises about daily practice
common_mistakes.correction_principle: treat the required cultural premise as part of the evidence, and mark the reading as unavailable when the premise is missing

instructional_purpose: Separates non-resemblance figurative transfer from resemblance-based metaphor and supplies a named inventory of the semantic links that license each transfer. Trains the learner to name the licensing link and its direction rather than merely notice that a word is used non-literally.
concepts_taught: المجاز المرسل as transfer licensed by a link other than resemblance
the licensing link (العلاقة) as the object to be named in every analysis
part-for-whole and whole-for-part as a mirrored pair
place-for-contents and contents-for-place as a mirrored pair
cause-for-effect and effect-for-cause as a mirrored pair
former-state and future-state naming as a mirrored temporal pair
directionality: which side is named and which side is intended
the exclusion clause: a resemblance basis removes the case from this class
the claim that the chosen part or state is functionally salient rather than arbitrary

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Non-resemblance transfer is licensed by a nameable semantic link between the word used and the meaning intended; if no link can be named, the case is not in this class.
The links form four mirrored pairs and each member is directional, so naming the link without naming its direction underdetermines the analysis.
The inventory of links is exactly eight.
The element selected in a part-for-whole transfer is normally the one functionally implicated in the predicate.
The section on the cause link tabulates a specimen under one link, then reverses the classification in the following prose and reassigns it to the mirror link, leaving the table uncorrected.
The contents-for-place link is illustrated with a specimen the lesson itself analyses inconclusively, and that specimen is nevertheless entered under that link in the summary table.
Assignment between the place link and the contents link is acknowledged to depend on what the analyst treats as emphasised, so it is not determinate.
Several canonical anchors for these links are scriptural, and some of them are classically contested between a figurative-transfer analysis and an elided-annexation analysis.
The rhetorical payoff of the transfer is conciseness plus foregrounding of the function named by the transferred word.

recognition_criteria: a token whose literal denotation cannot satisfy the predicate it stands under

exclude a resemblance basis, which would select metaphor instead
exclude a coherent literal reading, which would select the metonymy class instead
name the intended sense
name the licensing link and state its direction
if no inventory link fits, withhold the classification

the direction of transfer must be determinable from the context
the predicate or governor must be the element that rules out the literal sense
exceptions: a transfer resting on resemblance belongs to metaphor no matter how conventional it is

contrasts: part named versus whole named
place named versus contents named
cause named versus effect named
former state named versus future state named
non-resemblance transfer versus resemblance-based metaphor

common_mistakes.pattern: swapping the part-for-whole and whole-for-part labels

instructional_purpose: Moves indirection from the level of word meaning to the level of who is being addressed: a grammatically general or third-person utterance aimed at one specific hearer present in the situation. Catalogues the syntactic frames that carry this and the social reasons a speaker chooses it over direct address.
concepts_taught: التعريض as indirect address, set against التصريح as direct address
third-person or generic syntax carrying a specific second-person target
generic relative and conditional frames standing in for an imperative
indirect praise by negating the contrary quality
social functions: criticism without confrontation, praise without flattery, direction without a command form, and deniability for the speaker
recurrent carrier patterns including impersonal reporting frames, generic definite nominal statements, rhetorical questions and praise of an absent third party
non-verbal realisation through gesture or silence
the discriminating question separating indirection of the addressee from indirection of the meaning

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A grammatically general utterance can carry a specific addressee; the target is fixed by the situation and by nothing inside the sentence.

Recurrent carriers are generic relative clauses, conditional frames substituting for imperatives, impersonal reporting frames, generic definite nominal statements, rhetorical questions with a settled answer, and praise of an absent party.
A negated antonym functions as indirect praise of the quality it denies the absence of.
The same string is a proverb in one setting and indirect address in another, so the classification is a property of the utterance in situation and not of the sentence.

This device leaves the meaning transparent and the addressee implicit, while the neighbouring metonymy device leaves the addressee transparent and the meaning implicit; the two may co-occur in one sentence.
Gesture and silence count as realisations of the device.
Indirection preserves face for both parties and leaves the speaker room to deny that a specific person was meant.
Indirect address serves praise and approval as readily as criticism, so the device is not intrinsically adversarial.

recognition_criteria: a generic relative clause whose description is satisfied by exactly one person present in the situation
a conditional or generic frame occupying the discourse slot where a command was expected
an impersonal reporting frame introducing a normative claim
a definite generic nominal subject carrying a normative predicate
an interrogative whose answer is already settled by the situation
a mismatch between the grammatical person of the utterance and the participant it is aimed at
procedures: ask whether the surface is generic or third-person
ask whether one specific present participant satisfies the description
ask whether the situation makes the mapping unambiguous
name the speech act actually performed: direction, criticism, praise or approval
distinguish indirection of the addressee from indirection of the meaning before naming the device
conditions: a contextually salient target must exist and be present or otherwise relevant
the situation must make the intended mapping recoverable to that target
the generic statement must be independently true, which is what preserves deniability
exceptions: a general statement with no situationally salient target is a proverb or a maxim, not this device
the device may be realised without words, so absence of an utterance does not exclude it
contrasts: direct naming of the addressee versus generic or third-person framing
indirection of the addressee versus indirection of the meaning
imperative form versus conditional or generic substitute
explicit praise versus praise by negating the contrary

common_mistakes.pattern: treating every general statement as this device
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the device requires a specific situationally salient target and a context that makes the mapping clear
common_mistakes.correction_principle: require an identified present target before assigning the label; without one the sentence is only a general truth

common_mistakes.pattern: assuming the device is always hostile
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the same frames are used for praise, for assignment of a task and for approval
common_mistakes.correction_principle: read the speech act off the situation rather than off the indirect form

common_mistakes.pattern: overlooking realisations through gesture or silence
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the lesson treats non-verbal signalling as within the device when the context fixes the meaning
common_mistakes.correction_principle: attend to the communicative act, not only to the sentence, when the context is explicit

common_mistakes.pattern: conflating this device with the meaning-level metonymy device because both are called indirect
common_mistakes.why_wrong: they leave different things implicit, one the intended quality and the other the intended person
common_mistakes.correction_principle: ask whether what is hidden is what is meant or who is meant, and let the answer pick the device

misleading_shortcuts: treating every generic relative clause as indirect address
assuming the device always carries criticism
assuming it must be verbal
assuming a sentence can be classified from the string alone without a situation
treating the clean two-way split against the metonymy device as a settled classical boundary rather than a teaching dichotomy

nahw_relevance: medium — the carriers are genuine syntactic frames: generic relative clauses, conditional structures, generic definite nominal sentences, negated predicate adjectives and interrogative frames, all of which the learner must parse before the pragmatic layer applies
tutor_drill_relevance: medium — direct-to-indirect rewriting drills are mechanically checkable, but recognition drills need an authored situation because the string alone underdetermines the reading
rich_hover_relevance: low — no token carries the signal; at most a discourse-level note can be attached to a generic relative head

required_evidence: per occurrence: the generic or third-person frame, an identified situational target, and discourse evidence that the target is present or salient; none of this is recoverable from an isolated sentence, so per-occurrence application needs a discourse window and a participant list

proposed_new_units.summary: A discriminator over generic and third-person frames that asks whether a specific discourse participant is the intended target, listing the carrier frames and the situational evidence each one needs.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: The genuinely new material for u-n10 is narrow: a generic relative head may have a specific individual as its intended referent, fixed pragmatically rather than syntactically, and u-n12 gains the observation that such frames bind to a participant across turns. The frame inventory and the social-function account have no home in the catalogue, and u-n11 is touched only because the classical status of the device is itself disputed.

new_capability_required: pragmatic addressee resolution: a way to record that the intended target of a syntactically generic expression is a specific discourse participant, with the situational evidence attached; no current unit consumer represents speech-act targets

instructional_purpose: Treats a deliberate break in the expected continuation of person, number or tense across a stretch of discourse as a licensed stylistic device rather than as an inconsistency to be repaired, and pairs each direction of shift with the effect claimed for it.
concepts_taught: الالتفات as a shift running against the expected continuation
shift in grammatical person
shift in grammatical number
shift in tense or mood, including into the imperative
directionality of the shift and the effect claimed for each direction
simultaneous shifts on more than one dimension in a single utterance
functions: renewal of attention, escalation, modulation of proximity and distance, emotional colouring, argumentative challenge
the methodological stance that an apparent inconsistency in high literary and revealed text should be examined for purpose before being called an error
the inflectional evidence a reader uses to detect a shift

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A break in the expected continuation of person, number or tense is a licensed device when it serves a rhetorical effect, and is defined precisely as running against what the surface would otherwise require.
Three dimensions of shift are recognised: person, number, and tense or mood.
The direction of the shift determines the effect: moving toward the addressee raises confrontation and proximity, moving toward the absent person raises distance and objectivity.
One utterance may shift on two dimensions at once, so a single label per instance can be inadequate.
The lesson's own classification exercise forces one dimension label on a specimen its prose analyses as a double shift, so the taxonomy is not applied consistently within the lesson.
Apparent inconsistency in classical and revealed text is to be presumed intentional.
The device is claimed to be far more frequent in Arabic than the equivalent would be in English, and translation routinely neutralises it, so it must be studied on the Arabic.
Use of a plural first person where a singular referent is speaking is treated as a meaningful number shift rather than as a conventional register choice.

recognition_criteria: a change in subject-agreement person or number across adjacent predicates that share a referent
a switch between a pronoun series for one person and a series for another while the referent stays constant
a switch from perfective narration to imperfective within the same event line
a switch from a declarative or interrogative into an imperative aimed at the same participant
the absence of any referent change that could otherwise explain the break
an attached or independent pronoun whose person does not match the participant framing established a clause earlier
procedures: establish what the expected continuation was
locate the break and name the dimension on which it occurs
confirm that the referent did not change, which is what separates the device from ordinary reference tracking
check whether more than one dimension shifted at once
state the effect the shift achieves
conditions: the referent must be constant across the break
the break must be unexpected given the pattern established before it
a purpose must be assignable, otherwise the shift is not evidence of the device
exceptions: a genuine change of referent explains the change of person and is not this device
not every discontinuity is deliberate, since ordinary and non-edited text can simply be inconsistent
contrasts: person shift versus number shift versus tense shift
deliberate shift versus agreement error
movement toward the addressee versus movement toward the absent person
collective framing versus individual accountability in number shifts
narration in the perfective versus vivid narration in the imperfective

common_mistakes.pattern: reading the shift as a grammatical error
common_mistakes.why_wrong: in edited classical and revealed text the break is deliberate and carries an effect
common_mistakes.correction_principle: look for an assignable purpose before treating a break as a mistake, while still allowing that unedited text can simply be inconsistent

common_mistakes.pattern: expecting the device to be rare and therefore missing instances
common_mistakes.why_wrong: the frequency of the device in Arabic is much higher than the reader's English-based expectation
common_mistakes.correction_principle: calibrate expectation to the language rather than to translation habits

common_mistakes.pattern: assigning a single dimension label when two dimensions shifted together
common_mistakes.why_wrong: person, number and tense can move simultaneously in one short utterance
common_mistakes.correction_principle: check every dimension separately before naming the instance

common_mistakes.pattern: identifying the shift and stopping there
common_mistakes.why_wrong: detection without an account of the effect leaves the analysis incomplete and unfalsifiable
common_mistakes.correction_principle: always pair the located break with the effect it achieves in that context

common_mistakes.pattern: studying the device through translation
common_mistakes.why_wrong: translations commonly smooth the shift away and make it invisible
common_mistakes.correction_principle: work from the Arabic text and treat the translation as unreliable evidence for this device

misleading_shortcuts: flagging every person change as the device without checking referent constancy
assuming one instance carries exactly one dimension label
assuming any effect from the function list can be attached to any shift direction
treating a first-person plural as automatically a number shift rather than a register convention
assuming that because the device is common, every discontinuity is intentional

independent and attached pronoun series
perfective, imperfective and imperative stems

nominal and verbal sentence structure

sarf_relevance: medium — recognition runs entirely on inflectional exponents, namely subject-agreement affixes, pronoun series and the perfective, imperfective and imperative stems, although the lesson teaches none of that morphology and only consumes it
nahw_relevance: high — referent constancy across clauses, pronoun binding, and the discourse-level expectation of consistent framing are exactly the machinery the device breaks, and the break is only visible against that machinery
tutor_drill_relevance: high — detection over a supplied passage is mechanically checkable given the inflectional features; naming the effect is not checkable and should stay a discussion item
rich_hover_relevance: medium — a hover can state the person, number and tense of a token, which is the raw evidence, but the discontinuity judgement needs a span rather than a token, so a per-token hover can only feed the analysis and never conclude it
corpus_pvn_relevance: v entries carry most of the signal because person, number and tense exponents sit on the verb; p entries for independent and attached pronoun forms whose series membership is the other half of the evidence; n entries only where a full noun re-introduces a referent that had been pronominal
required_evidence: per occurrence: two or more predicates or pronouns over the same referent inside a bounded span, their person, number and tense features, a demonstration that the referent did not change, and an explicit span definition; a single token can never evidence this device
uncertainty_flags: school-dependent: narrower classical definitions restrict the device to shifts among speaker, addressee and absent person, while the three-dimension version taught here is the broader formulation
the lesson's own exercise assigns one dimension label to a specimen its prose calls a double shift
effect attribution is interpretive and cannot be certified from the text alone
the blanket presumption of intentionality is unsafe as an automatic rule outside edited classical and revealed text

proposed_new_units.summary: A span-level consistency check over person, number and tense features for a constant referent, which flags a licensed break, records its dimension and direction, and separates a licensed break from an agreement error by requiring referent constancy.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 gains genuinely new material here, namely that cohesion can be maintained across a deliberate break in framing and that the break itself is a cohesion signal; u-n10 gains the case where person changes without a referent change; u-s09 is only consumed, since the inflectional layering is used as evidence and not taught. What none of them carries is the span-level consistency check plus the licensed-exception clause, which is what makes the phenomenon checkable.

new_capability_required: effect attribution has no consumer interface: detection itself fits pattern_consistency over a span, so only the interpretive half of the lesson is unrepresentable and should be kept instructional
